batching.summary:
I did this step on top of the two earlier, unfinished attempts (saved in git between 6fab3bf and HEAD). I kept most of their work and fixed what was wrong. Nothing was committed or pushed.

WHAT I FOUND IN THE EARLIER WORK. It mostly worked. The verbs `variations` and `card-time`, the ledger and allowance, the sheet, the skills, agents and workflow were all there, and 3 batches had already run on the rented cards. Five things were wrong:
1. The check before drawing only compared settings, and that was not enough. In the first real moss batch 5 of 10 variations showed nothing on the card, and in the first cracks batch 5 of 10 came out alike.
2. "amount" could only make wear weaker, never stronger. Its "saved" value was also a guess.
3. If a command was cut off (for example by a time limit) while it waited for the cards, the ledger lost card time that had really been billed.
4. The plugin's example file was the cracks batch in which half the variations came out alike.
5. The text said "version" in some places and "variation" in others (one word for each thing is the rule).

WHAT I ADDED OR CHANGED
1. A free scout (`variations scout FILE.json`). It draws the same batch on this computer, tiny (240 x 160, 8 samples, about 40 s for the canal lock), costs no card time and does not count as a batch. `plan` and `run` then drop, before any card, every variation the scout found alike, each with a plain sentence.
   - I matched it against the two real card batches it had to agree with. With its own limits (0.75 and 0.3%, now house numbers marked measured) it called exactly the same 22 pairs "nearly the same" as the cards did, and no others.
   - It only uses a scout of the same scene and the same settings.
   - It also reads what the saved scene really has for each dial. The sheet shows this under the baseline, and the settings check compares against it.
2. `amount.<layer>` and `master` now multiply what the saved scene has: 0 to 2, where 1 means as saved. A batch can now try more wear as well as less.
3. `make --range KEY LOW HIGH` spreads a dial only over the part of its range that shows.
4. The ledger is safe against cut-off commands:
   - Every job gets a "sent" line the moment it goes out, and it counts at its estimate until the billed seconds arrive. `rent run` and `render` do the same.
   - The run folder keeps `run-state.json`, and `variations collect RUN-FOLDER` finishes a cut-off batch without sending anything again.
   - A failed upload still writes the small jobs it already ran.
   - The ledger file is locked while a line is written, so helpers writing at the same moment never mix their lines.
5. Writing:
   - "Variation" is now the one word everywhere the rule appears. The rule page `batched-rounds-and-card-time.md` is rewritten with a worked example first.
   - The scout, `--range` and `collect` are now in the REQUIRED block of the three skills, the tips guide, the builder, integrator and checker agents, and the workflow.
   - The example file is now the real proof batch. DEVIATIONS.md and both READMEs record what changed.

THE PROOF ON THE CARDS (small canal lock, 2 cameras, Cycles 600 x 400, RTX 4090s)
- I made 10 variations of the cracks-and-chips wear, with crack density spread from 0.6 to 1 and its strength from 0.6 to 2. I scouted them here for free first.
- Two earlier files each had one pair too alike in the scout, so they never went to a card. The third file scouted clean.
- On the cards: 3 jobs sent at the same time, 22 pictures, and all 10 came out measurably different, as the scout had said. The closest pair differed by 0.76 to 0.78 of 255 on average and in 0.46 to 0.57% of pixels, just above the limits.
- Card seconds: 178 in all, about US$0.05 (an estimate, not a bill). The plan had estimated 208.

1. `explainer-film-place renderer-for` (expect CYCLES). One sweep of every planned change, then one look: small portrait previews of the three views under three lights (flat, side, wet). Agents that did not build it, never given builder reports: place-checker in look, structure (their own ray scripts), process (money, ledger, privacy, leftover preview cameras), a blind reader on half-size pictures (reading test at least 12 of 16 features), then a skeptic who merges and ranks. Files carry a two-digit log number and plain words. Waiting on the person: the story calls (era, time of day, reference look), and a yes to painting. For that I would run `paint_request.py price` at fal's live rate (about 44 US cents for one 2k repaint with a style picture at 4.8 cents a megapixel in October 2026; prices move) and ask once. The later stages (plates, paint, pages, film, finish, and the script, fact-check and voice steps) are not started.

Structure changes need no picture: rerun construction, combine (plain and reverse, idempotent) and the audit. Wear and shape changes go through scout, then one batch. Camera changes go through plan_shot and check-shot, one problem at a time. Every report quotes measured numbers.

HOW I CHECK THE RESULT
Measured: preflight place exit 0, construction and scale lines, normal-map direction, the picture measures, and the stale-audit hash. Judged by fresh critics and the person's eyes: whether wear reads designed rather than photographic, whether boats read as boats and crates as fish crates at 300 px, and period accuracy of every object.

12. HOW I TEST CHANGES (cheapest first)

3. Free scout: `explainer-film-place variations scout FILE.json` draws the batch here, tiny (240 x 160), and names the variations that would not show. It is not a batch.
4. Batches on the card, only after the scout, inside the allowances. For each unsure change, about 10 settings far apart (`variations make --keys ... --range KEY LOW HIGH --count 10`), then `plan` (free), then `run FILE.json --where rented --helper NAME --role builder --ledger LEDGER` (up to 3 jobs at once, 600 x 400, one labelled sheet with measures and card seconds). - soot under the canopy and on chimneys (dials.grime.soot_under_shelter, runoff_streaks);
- moss on coping and shed brick (dials.moss_and_algae.cover, damp_need, shade_need);
- cracks and chips on brick (dials.cracks_and_chips.*);
- weeds and rubbish in ballast and yard (look lived_in versus neglected, master 0.6 to 1.6);
- shapes by a script hook (variation_hook.py): signal post lean, number of slipped slates, lamp lean.
5. Every card job lands in the ledger; I report card seconds, batches, variations dropped before drawing and flagged after.
6. I change the kit's code never. If I did, `python3 kit/calculators/tests/run_all.py` first.
